To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fully convolutional networks can be applied to spatially dense per-pixel prediction tasks and that they outperform the prior art on semantic segmentation.

fully convolutional networks can achieve state of the art results in semantic segmentation by themselves, without the use of any postprocessing or other techniques, that the combination of a shallow layer for appearance and a deep layer for context is a powerful architecture for dense prediction tasks, that it is possible to transfer the learned representation of one classification task to another, and that the resulting model can achieve state of-the art results in semantic scene understanding, while being fast enough for real-time deployment.
fully convolutional networks are powerful, flexible, and efficient models that can be trained end to end to produce accurate predictions.

convolutional networks, designed and trained for object classification, when applied to pixel-by-pixel prediction, achieve state of the art performance in semantic segmentation.
